results.identification: A secondary, bullet‑point summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2005 General Election manifesto titled “Forward, Not Back,” derived from the manifesto published by the Labour Party in April 2005.
results.evidence: The heading says “Labour Party Manifesto 2005: Summary (under 500 words)” and the text uses the 2005 Labour slogan “Forward, not back.” It lists hallmark 2005 Labour policies: ID cards, a points‑based immigration system, Academies expansion (200 by 2010), NHS 18‑week referral‑to‑treatment target, CO2 cuts (−20% by 2010; −60% by 2050), commitment to 0.7% ODA by 2013, the 2012 Olympics legacy, BBC Trust and digital switchover (2008–2012), and Building Schools for the Future.

results.identification: A bullet‑point summary of the UK Conservative Party’s 2005 General Election manifesto, known as “Timetable for Action,” produced by the Conservative Party (UK).
results.evidence: Mentions signature 2005 Tory themes and pledges: “cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes”; Australian‑style points‑based immigration and a British Border Control Police; oppose the EU Constitution and the euro; restore the earnings link for the Basic State Pension; scrap university tuition fees; reclassify cannabis to Class B; 20,000 extra prison places and honesty in sentencing; end central NHS targets, restore matrons, funding to follow the patient; halve council tax for over‑65s; extend Right to Buy; repatriate fisheries policy; ‘English votes for English laws’; and a first‑month ‘Timetable for Action’—all hallmark policies of the UK Conservative Party’s 2005 manifesto under Michael Howard.

results.identification: A condensed, bullet‑point summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2005 General Election manifesto (“The Real Alternative”), produced as the party’s official ‘manifesto in 500 words’ briefing and circulated on the Liberal Democrats’ campaign materials/website (libdems.org.uk) during the 2005 campaign.

results.identification: A bullet‑point summary of the UK Independence Party (UKIP) manifesto for the 2005 UK general election, derived from UKIP’s official 2005 manifesto.

results.identification: A policy summary/mini‑manifesto of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2005 General Election manifesto (England) — published by the Liberal Democrats.
results.evidence: Signature Liberal Democrat 2005 pledges appear throughout: replace Council Tax with a Local Income Tax; abolish university tuition/top‑up fees; introduce a 50% income tax rate only above £100,000; scrap ID cards to fund 10,000 more police; allow asylum seekers to work; extend STV voting; oppose replacing aging nuclear plants; carbon tax to replace the Climate Change Levy; Iraq withdrawal tied to the UN mandate; strong devolution note that policies mainly apply to England.

results.identification: A condensed summary of the UK Independence Party (UKIP) UK General Election manifesto from the mid‑2000s, specifically the 2005 UKIP General Election manifesto.
results.evidence: Repeated core planks associated with UKIP mid-2000s manifestos: immediate withdrawal from the EU by repealing the ECA; exit the CAP/CFP and reassert control of UK waters; replace VAT with a domestic sales tax (only possible outside the EU); equal treatment for EU and non‑EU migrants and a near‑zero net immigration target with embarkation controls; scrapping EU measures like the Working Time Directive and limits on supplements/herbals; charge EU students full overseas fees; Commonwealth/North America/Asia trade focus; citizen‑initiated national referendums at a 5% threshold; repeal the Human Rights Act; abolish English regional assemblies; rural policies like considering restoration of the Milk Marketing Board; halt wind turbines, push new nuclear and clean coal; strong NATO alignment and disengagement from EU defense. Specific tax ideas (halve council tax; raise IHT threshold to £500k; reinstate pension fund dividend tax credits) and NHS ‘matron’/de‑bureaucratisation also match UKIP’s 2005 general election platform.

results.identification: A condensed summary of the Green Party of England and Wales 2005 UK General Election manifesto (often presented under the title “Real Progress: The Green Party Manifesto for a Sustainable Society”).
results.evidence: UK‑specific policy mix including: universal Citizen’s Income and Citizen’s Pension; Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax/UBR; Contraction and Convergence with specific 2010/2020/2030 CO2 cuts; return rail and the London Tube to public ownership; re‑regulate buses; road pricing and higher fuel duty; oppose national ID cards; proportional representation and a fully elected upper chamber; disestablish the state church and limit the monarchy; oppose the proposed EU constitution while advocating EU reform; withdraw troops from Iraq and decommission nuclear weapons; Zero Waste Strategy banning incineration; strong animal welfare and GM‑free stance; targets like 40% renewables by 2020 and a 10% road‑traffic reduction by 2010. These are hallmark Green Party of England & Wales positions from 2005.
